thread.title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs; chips stocks rise

author: Fred Imbert
title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs; chips stocks rise
text:
Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs; chips stocks rise CNBC 1 hr ago Fred Imbert © Andrew Burton/Getty Images The Nasdaq composite jumped to a record high on Wednesday as chip stocks followed shares of Advanced Micro Devices higher.
The tech-heavy index traded 0.2 percent higher at the open, building on records set in the previous session. The Nasdaq closed above 7,000 for the first time on Tuesday.

▲ 174.14 +1.89 +1.10% Advanced Micro Devices rose more than 5 percent on the back of a report that points out a security flaw in Intel processors. The report by The Register said the issue will require a significant security update of Linux and Microsoft Windows operating systems to work around it.
Nvidia's stock climbed 2.6 percent, following AMD's gains. Intel shares, meanwhile, declined more than 2 percent.
The S&P 500 also posted an all-time high, advancing 0.1 percent with tech rising 0.5 percent. The Dow Jones industrial average traded 16 points higher.
"The uptrend still has the support of positive intermediate- and long-term momentum," said Katie Stockton, chief technical strategist at BTIG, in a note. "However, sentiment is now overly bullish based on two measures highlighted below, which sets up the market for a pullback later in the month."
Investors largely shrugged off a tweet from President Donald Trump about North Korea's Kim Jong-Un. Trump tweeted on Tuesday that his "nuclear button" was "much bigger and more powerful" than the one controlled by the North Korean leader.
In economic news, the manufacturing ISM report on business and construction spending are both due out at 10 a.m. ET. The Federal Reserve is also scheduled to release a summary of its December meeting.
